title: CERT-In Vulnerability Note  CIVN-2026-0556
content:
CERT-In Vulnerability Note 
                                                                      CIVN-2026-0556
TCP Pre-Authentication Remote Corruption vulnerability in the Linux kernel: NoisyTCP
Original Issue Date:November  17, 2026
Severity Rating: HIGH
Software Affected
Linux Kernel versions prior to 6.12.117, 6.18.63, 7.3.4 and 7.4-rc2
Overview
A vulnerability has been reported in Linux Kernel which could allow, a remote unauthenticated attacker to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) condition on the targeted system.
Target Audience:
Users and administrators of Linux-based systems.
Risk Assessment:
High risk of denial-of-service (DoS) condition.
Impact Assessment:
Potential for a kernel crash, resulting in a denial-of-service (DoS) condition.
Description
The Linux kernel is the core component of Linux-based operating systems and is responsible for managing hardware resources, memory and essential system services.
This vulnerability exists in the Linux Kernel's TCP networking subsystem due to a race condition during lockless socket lookups. A remote unauthenticated attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending specially crafted TCP packets to the targeted system.
Successful exploitation of this vulnerability could allow an attacker to cause a kernel panic, resulting in a denial-of-service (DoS) condition on the targeted system.

Apply appropriate security updates as mentioned by the vendor:
